- Working impression: Migraine with aura is suspected based on migrainous features and family history (DDx supports high likelihood; possible status migrainosus given persistence >72 hours). 
- Important differentials to consider (from DDx, consistent with transcript):
  - Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST): Medium concern due to estrogen-containing OCP and new persistent severe headache with visual symptoms; no focal deficits reported.
  - Tension-type headache: Possible but less likely given photophobia and visual phenomena.
- Safety: No red flag neurologic deficits reported during teleconsult; however, persistent new severe headache warrants in-person assessment and fundoscopic exam. 
- Plan from visit: 
  - Arrange in-person appointment for full neurologic exam and fundoscopy; check blood pressure; review contraceptive suitability if migraine with aura confirmed.
  - Medication: Prescribed an NSAID “stronger than ibuprofen” (name not documented) with food; may also take acetaminophen (paracetamol). Dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Safety net: If headache becomes unbearable, worsens, or changes character, attend Emergency Department; may call clinic for further advice.

- Book in-person appointment for neurological and fundoscopic examination; check blood pressure.
- Start prescribed NSAID (name not documented) with food; may combine with acetaminophen (paracetamol). Doses/routes/frequencies not documented.
- Review need to change combined oral contraceptive if migraine with aura is confirmed.
- Emergency precautions: Go to ED if symptoms worsen, become unbearable, or new neurologic symptoms occur; contact clinic for advice as needed.
